problem.text: Attention assumed Q/K normalization was RMSNorm, including RMS-specific attributes and fused RoPE weights. LayerNorm also restricted affine parameters to the final-axis shape.

reasoning.text: The edits are coupled: LayerNorm weights are excluded from RMS-only fusion, separate normalization moves before RoPE, and multidimensional affine weights are applied after final-axis normalization.

impact.text: Adds a reusable Q/K LayerNorm path to all three attention backends without wiring a model architecture to it. The new dispatch condition also introduces a suspected regression for loaded RMSNorm weights.

source_notes.text: Read the LayerNorm introduction, normalization-fusion entry and head-norm parameter repair. They establish the previous identical LayerNorm forward methods, fused RMSNorm interface and inherited native reduction/bounds concerns.

Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” reports conversion failure attributed in discussion to tokenizer truncation. Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns extension loading; #29, “Auto-YaRN for Qwen3? Maybe even set it dynamically?”, concerns scaling policy. Their relationship to this task is inferred solely from attention/rope source-path overlap, not evidence that QK LayerNorm addresses those reports.

limitations: No PyTorch, CUDA kernel, model inference or repository tests were executed. Tensor truth-value and shape failures are source-based observations, not reproduced exceptions.
The scalar calculation uses Python double precision, not the implementation's half-precision intermediate operations, broadcasting machinery or GPU scheduling.
Whole-tree literal searches identify explicit consumers, not dynamic or external callers. No checkpoint-level validation or performance measurement establishes model compatibility or overhead.

chapters.title: Separate Q/K LayerNorm from RMSNorm fusion

claims.text: Attention now accepts RMSNorm or LayerNorm for Q/K. It still requires K norm when Q norm is supplied. RMSNorm retains epsilon equality checking and constant weight bias; the LayerNorm branch copies Q's layernorm_eps and sets the fused weight offset to zero. Separate calls use each LayerNorm object's own epsilon, so they do not require equal Q/K epsilon.

load exposes normalization tensors to RoPE only for RMSNorm. For LayerNorm they remain None. Each decode route reshapes Q/K to batch × sequence × heads × head_dim, normalizes separately when RoPE is absent or no fused normalization tensor is available, then applies rotation. V is not normalized. Existing standalone calls without RoPE already supplied params and requested half output; the new calls retain that preparation.

RoPE.apply forwards optional weights to a native kernel implementing RMS normalization, not centered LayerNorm. The wrapper requires half Q/K; native fused Q weights must be one-dimensional and head_dim long. Keeping LayerNorm outside this kernel avoids applying the wrong normalization formula and permits per-head affine weights, at the cost of separate operations; no speed comparison was measured.

LayerNorm.forward preserves the existing F.layer_norm call for rank-one weights. Otherwise it normalizes only the final axis without affine parameters, multiplies by w and optionally adds b. Thus a heads × head_dim weight can broadcast across batch and sequence without normalizing across heads. Loading, optional bias, cached float32 copies and final dtype selection are unchanged.

A scalar transcription with two heads [1,3] and [2,6], separate affine rows and epsilon 1e-5 produced approximately [-1,3] and [-1,7]. This illustrates final-axis normalization followed by head-specific affine transformation, not normalization across the combined head axes.

Explicit Q/K norm builders remain RMSNorm in Qwen3, Qwen3 MoE and Gemma3; Gemma3 retains its unit weight offset. Cohere and Cohere2 construct LayerNorm only for block input and final normalization, not Q/K. Their existing rank-one-weight path is unchanged. ParallelDecoderBlock consumes input_norm through forward; TransformerBlock likewise calls forward for its norms. No LayerNorm subclass or forward_torch caller appeared in the whole-tree searches.

The earlier parameter-overwrite defect remains removed: defaults are still confined to attention without head norms. Native reduction and padded-read concerns remain unchanged in rope.cu. LayerNorm bypasses native normalization, but still uses native rotation; the new RMSNorm truth-value failure can prevent ordinary Attention calls from reaching the fused kernel.

findings.description: The fallback condition tests an RMSNorm weight tensor's truth value rather than its presence.
findings.trigger: Loaded Attention with RoPE, Q/K RMSNorm and a weight tensor containing more than one element.
findings.expected_behavior: Skip standalone normalization and use the existing fused RMSNorm/RoPE path.
findings.actual_behavior: Each decode method evaluates not self.q_norm_tensor, which requests an ambiguous multi-element tensor truth value before RoPE. Attention.forward directly dispatches to these methods; Qwen3, Qwen3 MoE and Gemma3 supply the relevant norm objects. No-norm, no-RoPE and LayerNorm cases short-circuit differently.

verification.description: Traced load's tensor assignment, all three changed conditions, forward dispatch and explicit model norm builders.
verification.limits: No PyTorch execution reproduced the exception.

findings.description: forward_torch retains the old affine-shape contract.
findings.trigger: Call LayerNorm.forward_torch with multidimensional weights newly supported by forward.
findings.expected_behavior: Provide the same final-axis normalization and broadcast affine transformation as forward.
findings.actual_behavior: forward_torch still passes the multidimensional weight directly to F.layer_norm with a one-axis normalized_shape. It lacks the new broadcast path. Whole-tree search found no repository caller, so the observed reach is the alternative method interface, not demonstrated production execution.

verification.description: Compared both methods with the complete LayerNorm diff and searched for alternative-method callers.
verification.limits: No external caller or Torch shape-error execution established.

findings.description: Inherited native reduction and padded-input-read concerns are carried over.
findings.trigger: Direct fused RoPE normalization with nonuniform lane values; or rotation with padded head width, such as 80, or shorter partial-rotary frequencies.
findings.expected_behavior: Store one complete sum per warp and avoid input reads beyond logical frequency/weight arrays.
findings.actual_behavior: Every lane writes its shuffle-down result to one shared sum slot. inv_freq[t] and normalization half2 weight loads lack padding guards. The existing test directly reaches this kernel with width 80 and normalization on/off, bypassing Attention's new dispatch failure. LayerNorm avoids the normalization-specific operations but not the frequency read.

verification.description: Compared unchanged native code with its reduction helper, wrapper, direct test caller and task diff.
verification.limits: No GPU race detection or observed memory fault.

verification.description: Computed 64 launched x lanes for width 80, versus 40 full-width frequency entries.
verification.limits: Integer launch arithmetic only, not kernel execution.

annotation.summary: Adds standalone Q/K LayerNorm before RoPE and broadcast affine weights, while introducing a suspected RMSNorm dispatch regression and leaving the alternative LayerNorm method unchanged.

argv:
import math
x=[[1.,3.],[2.,6.]]; w=[[1.,2.],[3.,4.]]; b=[[0.,1.],[2.,3.]]; eps=1e-5
out=[]
for row,wr,br in zip(x,w,b):
 m=sum(row)/len(row); v=sum((z-m)**2 for z in row)/len(row)
 out.append([(z-m)/math.sqrt(v+eps)*a+c for z,a,c in zip(row,wr,br)])
print('last-axis normalization then per-head affine:',out)
print('head_dim=80: lanes',((80//2+31)//32)*32,'frequency entries',80//2)
